content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn how to make caramel, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Review the chemical stages of sugar syrup (15 minutes)
Step 2. Set the heavy-bottomed saucepan on the burner (30 seconds)
Step 3. Read a professional chef's blog post on temperature control (10 minutes)
Step 4. Watch a video on the difference between wet and dry caramel (12 minutes)
Step 5. Measure out exactly one cup of granulated white sugar (1 minute)
Step 6. Research the best types of sugar for caramelization (20 minutes)
Step 7. Clear off the kitchen counter workspace (5 minutes)
Step 8. Check that the kitchen thermometer is calibrated (3 minutes)
Step 9. Purchase a high-quality brand of sugar (1 hour)
Step 10. Learn how to identify the "hard crack" stage (15 minutes)
Step 11. Study the safety precautions for handling molten sugar (25 minutes)
Step 12. Find the digital thermometer in the kitchen drawer (2 minutes)
Step 13. Prepare an ice bath in case of skin contact (2 minutes)
Step 14. Organize all ingredients in small bowls (10 minutes)
Step 15. Print out a troubleshooting guide for grainy caramel (5 minutes)
Step 16. Test the stove burner for consistent heating (4 minutes)
Step 17. Look up the boiling point of sugar at your altitude (5 minutes)
Step 18. Clean the saucepan to ensure no impurities remain (6 minutes)
Step 19. Identify your current elevation above sea level (2 minutes)
Step 20. Pour the finished caramel onto a silicone mat (2 minutes)
Step 21. Measure out the cold butter and heavy cream (3 minutes)
Step 22. Adjust the recipe's target temperature for altitude (3 minutes)
Step 23. Wash your hands thoroughly (1 minute)
Step 24. Combine the sugar and water in the pan (2 minutes)
Step 25. Soften the butter to room temperature (45 minutes)
Step 26. Place a pastry brush in a glass of water for crystallization control (1 minute)
Step 27. Browse photos of "amber" vs "deep mahogany" caramel (10 minutes)
Step 28. Set the butter out on the counter (1 minute)
Step 29. Assemble the whisk and heat-resistant spatula (2 minutes)
Step 30. Check the expiration date on the heavy cream (1 minute)
Step 31. Locate the heavy cream in the refrigerator (30 seconds)
Step 32. Verify the battery level of the digital scale (1 minute)
Step 33. Sift the sugar to remove any large clumps (4 minutes)
Step 34. Memorize the visual cues for the "light amber" stage (10 minutes)
Step 35. Take a photo of the final result for your records (1 minute)
Step 36. Print a color chart of caramel stages (5 minutes)
Step 37. Slowly whisk the cream into the hot sugar (5 minutes)
Step 38. Check the pantry for all necessary supplies (10 minutes)
Step 39. Stir in the butter cubes one by one (4 minutes)
Step 40. Prepare the heavy cream by bringing it to room temperature (1 hour)
Step 41. Wipe the inside of the pan with lemon juice to prevent crystals (2 minutes)
Step 42. Clean up the stove and utensils (15 minutes)
Step 43. Heat the sugar over medium-low heat (12 minutes)
Step 44. Allow the caramel to cool slightly in the pan (8 minutes)
Step 45. Write down notes on what you learned during the process (10 minutes)
Step 46. Buy a fine-mesh sieve (30 minutes)
Step 47. Search for "Caramel 101" tutorials online (15 minutes)
Step 48. Ensure the kitchen area is well-lit (1 minute)
Step 49. Read the comments section of the recipe for tips (20 minutes)
Step 50. Bookmark a reliable caramel recipe (2 minutes)
Step 51. Set a timer for the cooling phase (30 seconds)
Step 52. Calibrate the kitchen scale (5 minutes)
Step 53. Fetch the heavy cream from the store (45 minutes)
Step 54. Monitor the sugar as it dissolves and changes color (10 minutes)
Step 55. Learn how to stop the cooking process with liquid (15 minutes)
Step 56. Open the heavy cream carton (30 seconds)
Step 57. Read a guide on treating sugar burns (10 minutes)
Step 58. Put on an apron and oven mitts (1 minute)
Step 59. Swirl the pan gently as the color darkens (3 minutes)
Step 60. Take out the trash (5 minutes)
